balance.argument_a: A single steeper interval can be noise, not a genuine trend change -- Model A's own track record can be checked directly: plugging Pass 3's day (13) into Model A's equation predicts NDVI 0.52, only 0.01 off the real measured 0.51, at the one point where Model A's prediction can be checked against a reading it never used to build itself. Its crossing day (19) gives 7 real days of buffer before the day-26 deadline.
balance.argument_b: Model B captures the field's most recent, accelerating decline (Pass 2 to Pass 3, days 8-13, the steeper -0.022/day slope), predicting an earlier crossing day (18) and an 8-day buffer -- one more day than Model A, a real 14.29% margin.
balance.margin_basis: Days of safety buffer (filing deadline minus the model's algebraically-solved threshold-crossing day) for each model, computed in cases/field-watch/sensitivity_model.py from Appendix B/D figures. Higher buffer wins.

modeling_assumptions.text: NDVI damage threshold for this claim (0.40 = 0.37 base + a 0.03 calibration allowance). Real burn/stress NDVI thresholds are not universal -- they are regionally and crop-type calibrated (S2).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The 0.03 calibration allowance flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5 (effective threshold 0.385-0.415); winner (Model B) does not flip across the swept range, margin ranges 12.02%-17.09%.

modeling_assumptions.text: The three passes' specific NDVI values (Appendix B) and the filing deadline (Appendix D) are this field's own authored claim data -- no public database of real per-field insurance-claim satellite readings exists.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not FLEX-swept (authored field data, not a stated numeric assumption).

sensitivity_note: None triggering SPEC §6's hardship threshold, but noted: this case's stakes are a farmer's real crop-insurance claim -- a genuine economic concern, not personal loss or family hardship. Framed throughout as a professional analyst's judgment call, not a crisis.

catalog.blurb: A crop-insurance analyst has two competing models -- built from the same three satellite readings -- predicting when a damaged field crosses its payout threshold, and has to decide which one is more defensible to put in the claim file before it closes.
catalog.skills_focus: Linear expressions & multi-step equations -- distributive property, combining like terms, solving for a variable, percent
